definitions.plain: How far next year's regular income would fall short of next year's regular costs if the city kept doing exactly what it does now. It is a forecast made before the budget is written, and the budget then has to close it.

definitions.plain: The part of a balanced budget where ongoing costs are paid with money that won't come back next year, such as savings from earlier years or a skipped deposit into the rainy-day fund.

definitions.plain: Under the City Charter, planned spending can't be more than expected income plus any other money the city chooses to use. That other money can be one-time money, so a budget can be legally balanced and still have a structural deficit.

source.doc: San Diego City Charter: Article VII, Section 69 (printed page VII.1), the budget 'shall be balanced such that proposed expenditures shall not exceed projected revenues and any other sources to balance the budget'
